Seoul; SK Hynix quarterly operating profit 83.3 trillion won, nearly seven times a year earlier (AP)

geo_headlines: STRIKE PREP AFTER MIDTERMS. The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that the US warned Gulf states to prepare for a possible short, intense military campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterms (Iran International). Asked Wednesday whether strikes could resume, Trump said anything is possible and that ending the war is a question of when he wants to end it (ABC News).

QATAR DRAFT DEAL ON THE TABLE. Qatari mediators gave Iran a new draft deal Sunday with a seven-day timeline of daily confidence-building steps and several guarantor countries; Tehran is expected to respond by the end of the week (Reuters). Israel voted Tuesday; exit polls show Netanyahu's Likud as the largest party, and he called it a chance to remove the Iran threat (Iran International).

OIL BACK UP. **December Brent $114.93 (+0.9%) and December WTI $101.60 (+1.7%) after Tuesday's drop of almost $2, lifted by the strike report and a Houthi claim, not confirmed by Saudi authorities, of a missile hit on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery (Bloomberg, Economic Times).** Gold $4,059 (-0.4%).

FUTURES MIXED, TECH FIRM. S&P 500 futures 7,769.25 (+0.14%), Nasdaq 100 futures 29,954.75 (+0.48%), Dow futures -0.2% (Bloomberg). Tuesday the S&P 500 rose 0.6% and chips 3.6%; Boeing fell about 11% and UPS rose 6% (Investopedia). Robinhood -8% premarket on an earnings miss; Visa beat estimates after the close (Bloomberg).

ASIA SURGES ON CHIPS. Kospi +6.8% to 6,023.73 as SK Hynix jumped 11.4% and Samsung 9.1%; Nikkei +1.1%, Taiex +2% (AP). Stoxx 600 -0.2% (Bloomberg). Consumer confidence rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 (Conference Board).

FED DECIDES TODAY. A hold at 3.75-4.00% is expected; 94 of 100 economists in a Reuters poll see no change (EBC). FedWatch as of Tuesday 10/27: December hike 81.9%. 10-year 4.99%, 2-year 4.70%, 30-year 5.30% (Treasury). Bank of Canada 9:45 AM, expected to hike to 2.50% (Reuters). After the close: Alphabet, Microsoft (StockTitan).
client_frame_short: Tech stocks rose again Tuesday and the Fed decides this afternoon, where a hold is expected with a December hike still likely. **The new wrinkle is Iran: a report says the US told Gulf allies to prepare for a short campaign after next week's midterms, even as Qatar pushes a seven-day peace plan, so oil is back near $115.** Microsoft and Alphabet report tonight. For clients: the market is pricing both paths; stay diversified and rebalanced, avoid big bets on either outcome, and let bonds near 5% do their job.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is a two-day tech rally running into a Fed decision and a sharper Iran headline.

What changed overnight: the Wall Street Journal reported that the US warned Gulf states to prepare for a possible short, intense military campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterms. Trump said anything is possible. At the same time, Qatar has given Iran a draft deal with a seven-day timeline, and Iran is expected to answer by the end of the week. Oil rose about 1% to near $115 Brent. Asian chip stocks surged after SK Hynix reported profit nearly seven times last year's; Korea's market rose almost 7%.

Where we stand: the S&P 500 rose 0.6% Tuesday and is about 1.2% below its October 6 record close. Chip stocks are up about 6.5% in two days. Consumer confidence jumped to 91.7 as gasoline prices eased. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.99%.

Today: the Fed is expected to hold at 3.75-4.00% after September's hike; markets put the odds of a December hike near 82%, so the tone of the statement matters more than the decision. Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close, the first big test of whether AI spending is paying off; Amazon follows Thursday with GDP and PCE inflation.

Why it matters: Iran now has two clear paths, a deal within weeks or renewed strikes after the election, and markets are not fully pricing either. That is a reason to stay balanced rather than bet on one outcome. A strike would most likely show up first in oil and shipping, less in diversified portfolios.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and keep bonds working at today's yields. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Tuesday 4.99%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Tuesday 5.30%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (now $114.93). Brent is there, and the strike risk is now explicitly dated to after November 3.
